newsitem.title: INDIA: India says would maintain 15-15.5 pct M3 growth.
newsitem.headline: India says would maintain 15-15.5 pct M3 growth.

text.p: Indian Finance Minister P.Chidambaram was quoted as saying on Wednesday that the growth of broad money supply would be maintained between 15 and 15.5 percent in order to keep inflation at low levels.

"Money supply should not exceed this limit. This coupled with prudent macro-economic management, can keep the inflation reasonably low," the minister was quoted by the United News of India (UNI) as saying in the southern city of Madras.
India's year-on-year inflation rate based on wholesale prices currently stands at 5.85 percent. A year ago, it was 4.4 percent.

Money supply growth based on year-on-year calculations stood at 16.6 percent in May, compared with 16.8 percent a year ago. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has set a 15-15.5 percent growth target for M3, or broad money supply.
Chidambaram said customs duty collections had been sluggish because of a slowdown in imports.
"Direct tax collections have been good. Excise is moderate. But customs duty collections are sluggish," he was quoted as saying. He did not give details.
India's imports grew six percent in 1996/97 (April-March), to $38.5 billion, compared with a growth rate of 19.2 percent in 1995/96.
Trade figures released on Wednesday said the April-May imports stood at $6.24 billion, marginally below $6.28 billion in the same period of 1996.
